Name: Época Porto
Tips: Nordic-organic sourdough plates. Arrive 08:15 to beat the queue.

Name: Hakko
Tips: Croissants + Turkish eggs. Copenhagen-style specialty coffee.

Name: São Bento Station
Tips: 20,000+ azulejo panels depicting Portuguese history.

Name: Porto Cathedral (Sé)
Tips: 12th-century fortress church. Cloister azulejos and miradouro out back.

Name: Café Santiago
Tips: Most iconic francesinha in Porto. Arrive before noon to skip the line.

Name: Capela das Almas
Tips: Facade covered in 15,947 blue-and-white azulejo tiles.

Name: Palácio da Bolsa
Tips: SWAPPED OUT for MMIPO - guided tour only, 45-60 min on someone else's schedule, 56 EUR for four. Salao Arabe took 18 years to complete. Still 3 min away if you change your mind - Tue-Sun 09:00-18:30, last entry ~17:00.

Name: Centro Português de Fotografia
Tips: Former prison building; spy-camera collection, good for kids.

Name: Café da Porta do Olival
Tips: 1853 cafe hiding a stretch of the 14th-century Fernandina wall.

Name: Jardim das Virtudes
Tips: Terraced picnic gardens on the Douro hillside. Locals bring wine and blankets.

Name: Passeio das Virtudes
Tips: Faces west - Porto's best hidden sunset spot before the cruise.

Name: Porto 6 Bridges Sunset Cruise
Tips: 18:45 departure timed for sunset. Book online in advance.

Name: MUU
Tips: Contemporary Portuguese, dry-aged beef. Book 1-2 weeks ahead.

Name: Avenida dos Aliados
Tips: City hall and the grand boulevard, lit up at night.

Name: Picha Café
Tips: Young locals' bar, solid cocktails.

Name: Igreja de Santa Clara
Tips: BEST ADDITION to the three Porto days. 5 min from the Se, tucked against the medieval Fernandina wall. Plain Gothic shell from the 1400s hiding one of the largest surviving expanses of Portuguese talha dourada - walls, ceiling and columns entirely sheathed in gilded oak. Reopened after a long restoration and far quieter than Sao Francisco. Daily 09:00-13:00 and 14:00-18:00. NO visits during Mass.

Name: Igreja e Museu da Misericórdia (MMIPO)
Cost Range: ~5 EUR full, reduced for students and 65+, free under 7 - verify
Tips: REPLACES Palacio da Bolsa at 14:45. Zero detour - you already walk down Rua das Flores at 14:30. Ticket covers both museum and church. Centrepiece is Fons Vitae c.1520, a Flemish panel showing Dom Manuel I and family kneeling at the crucified Christ. Also Portugal largest portrait collection, ~500 works. Verify prices at mmipo.pt.

Name: Igreja dos Congregados
Tips: WALK-BY 1 min - directly across from Sao Bento station. Azulejo facade by Jorge Colaco, same artist as the Sao Bento panels and Santo Ildefonso. Exterior is the point.

Name: Igreja dos Grilos (São Lourenço)
Cost Range: MASA museum - price and hours unconfirmed
Tips: WALK-BY 2 min - immediately below the Se terrace. Jesuit, built 1577-1622, Mannerist facade carrying the Tavora arms, founder buried inside. Houses the MASA sacred-art and archaeology museum but hours/price could not be confirmed - treat the interior as a bonus and the facade as the visit.

Name: Igreja de Santo Ildefonso
Tips: WALK-BY - Rua de Santa Catarina ends right at it. 1739 proto-Baroque church fronted with ~11,000 azulejos laid in 1932 by Jorge Colaco, scenes from the life of St Ildefonsus in deep cobalt. Third Colaco facade of the day. Interior is plain by comparison - the tiles are the reason.

Name: Mosteiro de São Bento da Vitória
Address: Rua de São Bento da Vitória 45, 4050-543 Porto
Tips: WALK-BY on the 17:45 Miragaia route. Vast 17th-century Benedictine monastery built on the medieval Jewish quarter. NOT a walk-in church any more - belongs to Teatro Nacional Sao Joao, interior opens for performances and scheduled tours only. Walk the facade then carry on 2 min to the Miradouro da Vitoria beside it.
